Her daughter awakened, healthy and whole. And from that day forward, Astrid's celestial tapestry dances across the northern sky, rippling with color as the wind of the heavens breathes across it. The gods named it Aurora, and it reminds all who see it that a mother's love can illuminate even the darkest night.

"What is this darkness that dares exist in my light?" the Sun roared, burning hotter to destroy it.

But the shadow only grew longer.

Curious, the Moon emerged from hiding beyond the horizon. She had always feared the Sun's fierce brightness, but now she saw the shadow and understood its gift.

"Dear Sun," she said softly, "the shadow is not your enemy. It is your child, born from your own light meeting the solid world. Without shadows, nothing has form or depth. Your light creates beauty precisely because it can be interrupted."

The Sun considered this wisdom and dimmed slightly, allowing shadows to dance across the Earth. From that day forward, the world knew contrast—light and dark, day and night, form and void—and in that balance, beauty was born.
